goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: unsanitized raw RSS/Atom content is stored as raw_html and cooked without sanitization, allowing <script>/<iframe>/onerror injection from attacker-controlled feeds

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `cook_method` of `:raw_html` where `Post#cook` returns `raw` without going through the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. In `Jobs::PollFeed`, RSS content is taken from `i.content` (after `CGI.unescapeHTML` and `.scrub`, which does not sanitize HTML) and passed into `TopicEmbed.import`, which stores it and later serves it. The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any attacker-controlled HTML/JS in the feed (e.g., `<script>`, event handlers like `onerror`, iframes) would be stored and executed when viewed. Therefore, the finding describes a real stored-XSS risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped URL interpolated into HTML attribute and body in TopicEmbed footer, allowing script injection via crafted embed URLs

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML anchor tag: `"#{url}"` and appended to `contents`. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows quotes and other characters inside the URL (e.g. `http://example.com' onmouseover='alert(1)`), breaking out of the `href` attribute and injecting script/handlers. This content is then stored via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`, so there is no sanitization step to mitigate the injection. The embed view also renders cooked content with `raw post.cooked`, making this exploitable XSS via crafted embed URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError on feed items lacking content/link tags, aborting the loop and permanently blocking all subsequent items (no retry, no per-item rescue)
Infinite 30-second reload loop on embed loading page with silently swallowed retrieval failures, causing unbounded job/request amplification and no error surfaced to user

adjudication.rationale: Yes. When `EmbedController#best` can’t find an existing embed (`topic_id` is nil), it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `embed/loading`. The loading view unconditionally does `document.location.reload()` every 30000ms. If retrieval never succeeds (network error, parsing error, remote 404, misconfig, etc.), there is no terminal state or error page, so the browser will reload indefinitely. Each reload triggers another request and another enqueued `:retrieve_topic` job. Although `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles actual retrieval work to once per 60s, the job enqueueing and HTTP reload loop still continues indefinitely and can amplify load with many embedded clients, with no user-visible failure surfaced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic setnx/expire in TopicRetriever can leave a Redis key with no TTL, permanently wedging the retrieval throttle for an embed URL

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently? the throttle uses two separate Redis calls: `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or loses connectivity after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will be left without a TTL. Subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail and treat it as "retrieved recently" forever, permanently wedging retrieval for that embed URL. This is a known non-atomic pattern; the diff introduces it exactly as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update path crashes with NoMethodError when the embedded post has been deleted, since embed.post is used without a presence check

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update branch does `post = embed.post` and, if `content_sha1` differs, immediately does `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and later `embed.update_column(...)`. There is no guard for `post` being `nil`. Although the migration sets `topic_embeds.post_id` to `null: false`, there is no foreign key, so the associated `posts` row can be deleted while the `topic_embeds` row remains. In that case `embed.post` returns `nil`, and calling `PostRevisor.new(nil)` / `revisor.revise!` will raise (likely a `NoMethodError`) when `PostRevisor` dereferences `@post`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import_remote fetches the URL before scheme/host validation and open-uri follows cross-origin redirects, creating an SSRF vector
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe an SSRF risk caused by fetching a URL via open-uri/open before properly validating it (including redirects). The golden focuses on PollFeed using SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without validation; the candidate describes the same underlying vulnerability pattern (unvalidated URL fetch leading to SSRF), albeit referencing import_remote and redirect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CGI.unescapeHTML double-decodes feed content before import, corrupting legitimate escaped entities and converting escaped HTML into live executable tags

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then imports it via `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. TopicEmbed creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook returns `raw` for that method, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. This means any entity-escaped markup in the feed (e.g. `<script>`) will be decoded into real tags and stored/rendered as raw HTML, enabling executable HTML/JS in the resulting post/embed. The diff does not show an actual *double* decode (only a single `unescapeHTML` is present), but the core issue—decoding entities into live HTML before storing/rendering as raw—is verifiably introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key computes a Redis key that is never used; a Last-Modified/ETag short-circuit was intended but dropped, causing the hourly poll to unconditionally fetch the whole feed and iterate every item even when nothing changed

adjudication.rationale: In the new scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed`, a `feed_key` method is defined that computes a Redis key (`"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(...)}`) but that method is never called anywhere in the diff. The `poll_feed` method always performs `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items` without any Last-Modified/ETag or other change-detection check. Given the `recurrence { hourly }`, this means it will fetch and process the full feed every hour regardless of whether it changed, and the presence of the unused `feed_key` strongly indicates an intended short-circuit/caching mechanism that is currently missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve synchronously runs the full Jobs::PollFeed feed poll inline, triggering a full feed download and import of all items on a single user's first view of an un-embedded article and holding a Sidekiq worker for the duration

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `perform_retrieve` directly invokes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs a synchronous `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` network fetch, parses the feed, and iterates all `rss.items` importing each via `TopicEmbed.import`. Since `TopicRetriever` is called from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` (a Sidekiq job), this means the feed download+full import can run inline within that Sidekiq worker during a first-time embed retrieval, potentially tying up the worker for the duration instead of scheduling the polling separately.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retrieved_recently? uses non-atomic SETNX followed by EXPIRE, so if the process dies between the two calls the Redis throttle key persists without a TTL, permanently blocking auto-retrieval for that URL and leaking keys without bound; should use a single atomic SET key val EX 60 NX

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is interrupted after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the key will be left without a TTL. After that, SETNX will always fail for that URL and the method will keep returning `true`, effectively blocking retrieval indefinitely and leaving orphaned keys in Redis. Using an atomic `SET retrieved_key 1 EX 60 NX` (or a transaction/Lua) would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import_remote and feed polling use open(url).read to download the entire remote response into memory with no size cap, which can balloon worker memory on large or misbehaving remote resources

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `open(url).read` and passes the full string into `Readability::Document.new(...)`, which necessarily buffers the entire remote response in memory with no size/timeout cap. In `Jobs::PollFeed`, it does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, which fetches and parses the remote feed from an unbounded IO (no explicit size limits). Both can lead to excessive memory usage (and potentially worker DoS) if the remote resource is very large or misbehaves.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 user loads in embed view: post.user.small_avatar_url and post.user.username are accessed per post without the User association being eager-loaded, causing up to ~5 extra queries per embed render on a high-traffic iframe endpoint with frequent cache misses

adjudication.rationale: The embed view does call `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` inside a loop, which could cause N+1 queries *if* the `user` association is not preloaded. However, the diff does not show how `@topic_view.posts` is loaded (the eager-loading behavior would be inside the existing `TopicView` implementation, which is not changed here). Since `TopicView.new(...)` and its query/preload strategy are outside the diff, the finding’s claim that the association is not eager-loaded is not verifiable from this change alone, and therefore is speculative rather than a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController enqueues a RetrieveTopic job on every cache miss while the 60s throttle is only checked inside the job, so bursts of first-views of the same URL produce many mostly no-op Sidekiq enqueues

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. There is no controller-side throttling/deduplication keyed by `embed_url`. The only 60s throttle is in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which is invoked inside the job (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` -> `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`). This means a burst of requests for the same new `embed_url` will enqueue many Sidekiq jobs; most will quickly no-op due to the Redis throttle, but they are still enqueued and processed, creating avoidable queue load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public CLI task signature removed: disqus:import drops the --category/-c option with no migration path, breaking existing callers invoking 'thor disqus:import -c'

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor explicitly removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and also deletes the logic that reads `options[:category]` and passes `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. With this change, invoking `thor disqus:import -c ...` will no longer accept `-c/--category` (Thor will treat it as an unknown option), which is a breaking change for existing callers, and no replacement or deprecation path is shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus:import task behavior changed to fetch live content via TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of importing from the export file, silently changing behavior and losing created_at preservation; dead links silently skip threads

adjudication.rationale: This is verifiable in the diff: in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the topic-creation step changed from `PostCreator.new(... raw: "[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})]", created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` fetches live HTML via `open(url).read` + `ruby-readability` and then calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post without passing `created_at` (so the post timestamp won’t match the Disqus export’s `t[:created_at]`). The “dead links silently skip threads” part is not supported by the diff (a dead link would more likely raise from `open(...)` unless rescued elsewhere), but the behavior change and loss of created_at preservation are real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported raw HTML bypasses sanitization/cooking pipeline: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for cook_method == raw_html and TopicEmbed.import stores content as-is with skip_validations, creating a stored XSS surface via the embed view's '<%= raw post.cooked %>'

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new cook_method enum with a :raw_html option and changes Post#cook to `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. TopicEmbed.import creates posts via `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`, so imported content is stored and later served verbatim as the cooked HTML. The embed view renders it using `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which will output any HTML/JS present in the imported content without sanitization. This creates a verifiable stored XSS surface for RSS/remote-imported content (especially via PollFeed, which uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` but does not sanitize HTML).

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed import path passes CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) with no tag/attribute filtering, and unescaping HTML converts safely-escaped entities in the source feed into live markup

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` builds `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore any HTML entities in the feed (e.g. `<script>`) will be unescaped into live markup and stored/rendered as raw HTML with no tag/attribute filtering, creating an XSS vector from untrusted feed content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Readability import path whitelists tags but not href attribute values, allowing javascript: URLs

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code uses `Readability::Document.new(..., tags: ..., attributes: %w[href src])`, which whitelists the presence of `href`/`src` attributes but does not (in this diff) validate or restrict their values/schemes. The resulting `doc.content` is then imported via `TopicEmbed.import` into a post created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` for `:raw_html`, bypassing Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative URLs starting with `/` and will not neutralize `javascript:` URLs. The embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so a malicious `href="javascript:..."` would be preserved and rendered, creating an XSS vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError on feeds without a content field (RSS 2.0 description-only feeds yield nil), aborting the whole poll; combined with sidekiq retry: false the failure is silent

embed.js postMessage origin check uses indexOf substring match instead of exact origin match, allowing lookalike origins (e.g., https://foo.co vs https://foo.com) to pass and inject discourse-resize messages
New dependencies ruby-readibility and simple-rss added only to Gemfile_rails4.lock, leaving primary Gemfile.lock out of sync, causing bundle validation failures for BUNDLE_FROZEN deploys and CI

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` to the main `Gemfile` and also updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock` accordingly. The proposed finding claims the dependencies were added only to `Gemfile_rails4.lock`, which is a misreading of the diff. Additionally, the diff does not show any `Gemfile.lock` file at all, so an out-of-sync primary lockfile and resulting `BUNDLE_FROZEN`/CI failures are not verifiable from this change alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Network fetches via open-uri in PollFeed and TopicEmbed have no open_timeout/read_timeout, which can hang Sidekiq workers indefinitely and exhaust the worker pool

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces network fetches using `open-uri` without specifying any `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. With no explicit timeouts, these Sidekiq jobs can block for a long time on slow/hung HTTP/DNS/connection reads, tying up worker threads and potentially exhausting the worker pool.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsanitized third-party HTML rendered raw (raw_html cook method and '<raw post.cooked>' in embed view) allows XSS via feed/embed content

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` mode where `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`return raw if cook_method == ...`). `TopicEmbed.import` builds `contents` from third-party RSS/Atom (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, then `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it as `raw` to `PostCreator` with `cook_method: raw_html`. In the embed UI, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders posts with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and for these imported posts `post.cooked == post.raw` (as asserted in the spec). There is no sanitization of the feed content before storing/rendering, so malicious HTML/JS in the feed (or embedded page content) can be persisted and executed, i.e., a verifiable XSS vector introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed#poll_feed crashes on feed items with nil content because nil.scrub raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire poll mid-loop

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item has `content` missing/blank (i.e., `i.content` is `nil`), calling `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, which would abort `poll_feed` and stop processing remaining items. There is no nil-check or fallback to another field (e.g., `description`) in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: String#scrub in PollFeed is not available on Ruby < 2.1, raising unconditionally on older runtimes

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. `String#scrub` was added in Ruby 2.1; on Ruby 2.0/1.9 this call would raise `NoMethodError` at runtime when polling a feed. The diff provides no guard/fallback, so this is an introduced compatibility defect if the app runs on <2.1 (and the repo even references 1.9-era constraints elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE throttle key in TopicRetriever can leave the key without a TTL if the process dies between calls, permanently throttling that embed URL

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, the throttle key is set with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only afterward given a TTL via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or an exception occurs between these two calls, the key may be created without an expiration. Since later calls treat any existing key as “retrieved recently” and return `true`, that embed URL could remain throttled indefinitely until the key is manually cleared.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage origin check in embed.js uses substring matching (indexOf) instead of equality, allowing forged messages from prefix origins

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is a substring check, not an exact origin match. If `discourseUrl` is something like `https://discourse.example.com/`, a message from a different origin whose string is a prefix of that (e.g. `https://discourse.example.co`) would pass because `indexOf` returns 0. This can allow non-Discourse origins to send `discourse-resize` messages and affect the iframe height. A strict equality check against the expected origin (or parsing `discourseUrl` to its origin) is needed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading view reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with no backoff, cap, or failure signal, creating an unbounded retry/DoS source when import never succeeds

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the page unconditionally runs `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);` with no cap, backoff, or stop condition. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., bad/unsupported URL, repeated failures, or settings/user missing), the iframe will keep reloading every 30 seconds indefinitely, repeatedly hitting the endpoint and potentially re-enqueueing work depending on timing, creating an unbounded retry/request loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve polls the entire feed synchronously inside a background job for every unmatched embed URL, causing duplicate import work and RecordNotUnique job failures

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (synchronously) before falling back to HTTP. This means every `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` execution for a missing `embed_url` can trigger a full feed fetch/parse and iterate/import *all* items (`PollFeed#poll_feed`), even though the caller is trying to resolve one URL. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic “check then create” (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!`) with a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`; concurrent PollFeed/retrieve runs can race and raise `RecordNotUnique`, causing job failures since it isn’t rescued.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Resize postMessage in embed layout breaks when request.referer is absent, rendering an empty targetOrigin and throwing so the iframe never resizes

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, a missing `request.referer` causes `URI(request.referer || '').host` to be `nil`, which will not match `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, so it raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` and the embed layout is never rendered. Therefore the layout’s `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` is not executed in the “referer absent” case described. (Separately, the code *does* appear to pass the full referer URL as `targetOrigin`, which may be invalid per the postMessage API, but that is not what the proposed finding claims.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: No error handling around feed parse/fetch in the scheduled poll job; malformed feeds or network errors are silently lost with retry: false and no logging/alerting

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no `rescue`/fallback around network failures (open-uri) or parse failures (SimpleRSS). The job also sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so transient exceptions won’t be retried by Sidekiq and the run will just fail (at best only re-attempting on the next hourly recurrence). While failures wouldn’t be truly “silent” (exceptions typically get logged by Sidekiq), it is correct that there is no explicit error handling/logging/alerting in the code and failures can cause missed imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Concurrent import race on embed_url check-then-insert causes RecordNotUnique job failures instead of being handled as expected deduplication

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`) but both `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` and `TopicEmbed.import` use a check-then-insert pattern: `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!` when blank. Under concurrency, two jobs/requests can both observe “no row” and then both attempt `create!`, causing an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or similar) exception. There is no rescue/retry/dedup handling around `create!`, so this would surface as job failures rather than graceful deduplication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No coverage that imported raw HTML content is sanitized — TopicEmbed.import stores feed HTML with cook_method: raw_html, bypassing sanitization, and the embed view renders it with raw post.cooked, creating an untested stored-XSS path

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `Post.cook_method` enum with a `:raw_html` mode, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly when that mode is set, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, passing feed/remote HTML (only URL-absolutized) straight into `raw`. The embed view then renders it as HTML via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. For RSS polling, `i.content` is unescaped and passed through with no sanitization; for `import_remote`, Readability restricts tags/attributes but does not guarantee XSS-safe URLs/values. Specs assert `post.cooked == post.raw`, reinforcing that no sanitization occurs and there is no test ensuring unsafe HTML is removed. This is a verifiable stored-XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController#best success tests verify mock wiring instead of behavior: the test expects TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve while the controller enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and never asserts the job payload; TopicView is fully mocked so real view rendering (avatars, post.cooked, post limit, header/footer logic) is unexercised

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders 'loading'; it never instantiates or calls `TopicRetriever` directly. However, the controller spec `it "tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found"` sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve`, and does not assert the enqueued job/payload. That expectation contradicts the controller implementation and would fail as written. The additional note that TopicView is mocked (thus not exercising view behavior) is also true but is more about test coverage quality than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed has zero coverage: every test stubs the method, leaving the URL fallback logic, nil-content handling of CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) (NoMethodError risk for description-only feeds), missing-user early return, and re-poll idempotency untested

adjudication.rationale: The new spec file `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` and, in the positive case, asserts `poll_feed` is called; it never exercises the actual `poll_feed` implementation (it stubs/expects the method instead). In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (common for RSS items that only provide `description`/`summary`), `i.content` may be `nil`, and calling `.scrub` on `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`. This is a concrete runtime-risk introduced in the diff and currently untested, along with the other internal branches (missing user early-return, URL fallback) the finding mentions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever tests stub out all real logic: retrieved_recently? is stubbed so the Redis setnx/expire throttling and 60s window are never tested, and perform_retrieve/fetch_http (already-embedded check, feed-polling fallback, missing embed_by_username return) are never exercised

adjudication.rationale: This is verifiable from the added spec. In `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, the “valid host” examples explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` (`topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false/true)`), so the real throttling code that uses `$redis.setnx`/`expire` and the 60s window is never executed in tests. The spec also never calls the real `perform_retrieve` implementation (it only sets an expectation that it is/ isn’t called), so the internal behaviors in `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` (already-embedded early return, feed polling fallback, and the `embed_by_username`/missing user return path) are not exercised by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer-host validation is never tested with a wrong referer: no test covers a referer host differing from embeddable_host (the primary reject path of ensure_embeddable) nor malformed referer URIs raising URI::InvalidURIError through the rescue

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the main rejection logic is `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and there’s also a `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` path. The added `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` covers: missing `embed_url`, missing `embeddable_host`, missing referer (`referer` nil), and a successful case where `referer` matches `embeddable_host`. It does not include any test where `request.referer` is present but has a different host than `embeddable_host`, nor a test where `request.referer` is a malformed URI that would trigger the `URI::InvalidURIError` rescue branch. So the finding about untested reject paths is verifiably true from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor#update_post change to @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) shipped with no test exercising either branch, including the skip_validations: true path used by TopicEmbed.import and normal revisions still validating

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a test that exercises the `skip_validations: true` path. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed’s content changes it calls `PostRevisor#revise!` with `skip_validations: true`, and `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` includes "Supports updating the post" which triggers that update flow. That will execute `PostRevisor#update_post` and hit the new `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` branch with validations disabled. Therefore the claim that no test exercises either branch (especially the skip-validations branch used by TopicEmbed) is not verifiably true from this diff; and lack of coverage for the normal-validations branch cannot be concluded from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import re-import path only tests the changed-content branch: the content_sha1 equality short-circuit (no revise, no update_column on identical content) and correct sha1 storage on creation are untested

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, TopicEmbed.import has three notable behaviors: (1) on first import it computes content_sha1 and stores it in TopicEmbed.create!, (2) on re-import with identical contents it should short-circuit (no PostRevisor.revise! and no embed.update_column), and (3) on re-import with changed contents it revises and updates content_sha1. The added spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb covers creation and the changed-content update ("Supports updating the post"), but does not exercise the identical-content path (where content_sha1 == embed.content_sha1), nor does it assert that the stored embed.content_sha1 equals Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents) on creation—only that a TopicEmbed row exists. So the finding accurately identifies untested branches/expectations introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus importer behavior change with no test: import path rewritten from locally-created permalink post to TopicEmbed.import_remote performing HTTP fetches, and the --category CLI option silently removed, breaking users who relied on it

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Disqus Thor task CLI option `--category` (`method_option :category` deleted) and deletes all logic that looked up `category_id` and passed it to `PostCreator`. In the same method, it replaces creating a local post with a permalink (`PostCreator.new(... raw: "[[Permalink](...)]", category: category_id)`) with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which performs an HTTP fetch (`open(url).read`) and imports remote content. This is a concrete behavioral/API change in the importer and will break users who relied on the `--category` option (Thor will no longer accept it). No tests are added/updated for the Disqus importer behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: TopicEmbed.import passes arbitrary feed HTML through with cook_method: raw_html, bypassing sanitization, and the embed view renders it with raw post.cooked, allowing malicious script tags/event handlers from the feed to be stored and served to all visitors

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In Jobs::PollFeed, `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is taken from the RSS/Atom feed and passed to `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import` creates the post via `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. The new `Post#cook` method explicitly returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked`, which for `raw_html` equals the unsanitized feed HTML. This is a stored XSS vector (e.g., script tags, event-handler attributes) that would be persisted and served to visitors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration default contradicts enum: db migration adds cook_method with default: 1 (raw_html) instead of 0 (regular), causing all existing and new posts to skip cooking entirely

adjudication.rationale: The finding assumes the Enum values are 0-based (regular=0, raw_html=1), but this codebase pattern strongly suggests they are 1-based. `Post.types` is defined with `Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)` and Discourse commonly stores `regular` as 1 in the DB for similar enums. Given `cook_methods` is `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and the migration sets `cook_method` default to 1, that aligns with `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. Therefore the diff does not verifiably cause all posts to skip cooking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attacker-controlled Referer header interpolated unescaped into inline JS in app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb via parent.postMessage('<%= request.referer %>'), allowing string/script context breakout injection; also duplicates origin state handled in embed.js
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same vulnerability: the attacker-controlled Referer header (request.referer) is directly interpolated into inline JavaScript without escaping, enabling XSS/script injection via context breakout.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host-validation logic duplicated between embed_controller.rb and lib/topic_retriever.rb with slightly different semantics (blank setting handling differs), risking drift in security-relevant rule

adjudication.rationale: The diff does contain host checks in both EmbedController#ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, but they are validating different things (referer host vs. embed_url host) for different layers of the flow. The claimed semantic difference for a blank embeddable_host is not actually present: in EmbedController a blank setting raises, and in TopicRetriever a nil/blank setting makes `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` true, so retrieval is also blocked. The “risking drift” aspect is speculative rather than a concrete defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) invoked directly and synchronously from TopicRetriever, coupling retriever to scheduled job internals and bypassing Jobs.enqueue

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. However, in this same diff `TopicRetriever` is invoked asynchronously via `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and then executed inside `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, so the feed polling call still happens in a background job context (not synchronously in the web request). Calling another job class' `execute` method directly may be an architectural smell, but the finding claims it as a concrete problem ("bypassing Jobs.enqueue" / incorrect coupling) and the diff does not demonstrate a functional bug or defect resulting from this; it will still work correctly and remains asynchronous overall due to the outer job.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embeddable user lookup duplicated identically in poll_feed.rb and topic_retriever.rb (User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first), risking drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff does contain identical user lookup logic in two places: `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` and `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` both do `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first`. However, this is just code duplication/DRY concern. It does not introduce a verifiable bug, security issue, or correctness defect in the change itself; the behavior is consistent and there’s no demonstrated “drift” problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: URL-scheme validation (^https?://) re-implemented inline in PollFeed#poll_feed instead of reusing canonical validator in topic_embed.rb

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows URL scheme checks in multiple places (PollFeed#poll_feed and TopicEmbed.import), but TopicEmbed does not define any “canonical validator” method to reuse—its validation is also an inline regex (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`). PollFeed’s similar regex is at most duplication/maintainability, not a clear bug or correctness/security defect introduced by the diff, and the finding’s premise (a canonical validator exists) is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) assumes i.content is non-nil; feeds with only description/summary but no content will raise NoMethodError, aborting the whole poll with retry: false and no error surfacing
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying bug: code calls `i.content.scrub`/`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assuming `i.content` is always present, but many feeds omit `content` (only have description/summary), causing a nil/NoMethodError crash. Golden additionally suggests a description fallback, which the candidate also implies by mentioning feeds with only description/summary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import mutates caller's contents string in place (contents << "\n<hr>..."), causing surprising behavior with frozen or reused strings

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."` appends to the *same String object* passed by the caller, mutating it in place. This is directly verifiable in the diff and can cause unintended side effects if the caller reuses `contents` after calling `import`, and it will raise an exception if a frozen string is passed (e.g., `"...".freeze` or other frozen-string sources). The method does not duplicate `contents` before modifying it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead translation key embed.permalink: "Permalink" added to server.en.yml but never referenced

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed.permalink` to `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and within the shown changes there is no reference to `I18n.t('embed.permalink')`. However, the claim that it is "never referenced" cannot be verified from the diff alone because the key could be used elsewhere in the existing codebase outside this patch. Also, an extra unused translation key is not a clear defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to pre-existing migration create_top_topics.rb, which will silently drop an existing top_topics table in replay/restore scenarios (data-loss footgun)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `CreateTopTopics` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing `top_topics` table before recreating it. That turns what would normally be a safe failure (table already exists) into a destructive operation if this migration is replayed or run against a DB that already has `top_topics` (e.g., restore/rebuild/migration-state mismatch), creating a real data-loss footgun.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Premature option-plumbing via untyped opts hashes across three layers (embed_controller, RetrieveTopic, TopicRetriever) with repeated validation and different error types at each hop

adjudication.rationale: The diff does pass an `opts` hash through Jobs::RetrieveTopic into TopicRetriever (`no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`) and does validation at multiple layers (controller checks referer/embeddable_host and raises Discourse::InvalidAccess; job checks presence and raises Discourse::InvalidParameters; TopicRetriever checks host/URI validity and just returns without raising). However, this is primarily an architectural/maintainability critique (“untyped opts hashes”, “repeated validation”, “different error types”), not a concrete bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change. The behavior remains coherent: invalid cases either raise in the controller or result in a no-op retrieval. Nothing in the diff shows this causing an actual failure or vulnerability by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw HTML import path bypasses the sanitization/cooking pipeline: cook_method == raw_html returns raw content verbatim, which is rendered with raw post.cooked in the embed view, allowing onerror/onclick handlers and javascript: hrefs from external RSS/Readability content to execute as stored XSS

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `cook_method` option where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` using external content (`SimpleRSS.parse(open(...))` with `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and `Readability::Document`’s `doc.content`). Neither path sanitizes against dangerous attributes/URLs (e.g., `onerror`, `onclick`, `javascript:`), and `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href`/`src` without filtering. The embed view then renders `post.cooked` with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so malicious HTML from RSS/remote pages can execute as stored XSS. This is directly verifiable from the added `cook_method` bypass and raw rendering in the new embed feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Readability's tag filtering is not sanitization: it does not strip attribute content like event handlers or javascript: URIs, so malicious attributes survive into rendered embeds

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `ruby-readability` to extract HTML and explicitly allows tags/attributes including `href` and `src` (see `Readability::Document.new(..., tags: ..., attributes: %w[href src])`). The extracted `doc.content` is then imported into a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Since there is no protocol sanitization shown, a `href="javascript:..."` (or other dangerous URI scheme) can survive Readability's filtering and will be emitted as raw HTML in the embedded page, creating an XSS risk. (Event-handler attributes like `onclick` may be removed by the attribute whitelist, but dangerous values inside allowed attributes are not addressed.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Modifying already-shipped migration create_top_topics to add force: true makes re-runs destructive, silently dropping all top_topics data via DROP TABLE IF EXISTS

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `CreateTopTopics` from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` causes the adapter to drop the table first (e.g., `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics`) before recreating it. If this migration is ever executed against a database where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., a re-run/redo, or a DB where the table was created out-of-band), it will silently delete all `top_topics` data. That destructive behavior is introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false causes a full table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PostgreSQL < 11, blocking all reads/writes on the largest table for minutes

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` with `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-NULL default generally rewrites the whole table and takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration, blocking reads/writes. Since `posts` is typically one of the largest tables, this is a concrete operational risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed job crashes with NoMethodError on feed items lacking content (CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) when content is nil)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item has no `content` element (common in RSS/Atom where content may be `description`, `summary`, etc.), then `i.content` will be `nil` and calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`. There is no nil check or fallback in the diff, so the job can crash on such items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed accesses i.content which may not exist for valid RSS feeds since simple-rss exposes description instead of content

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. For many valid RSS 2.0 feeds, `SimpleRSS` items commonly expose `description` (and sometimes `content_encoded` for `content:encoded`) rather than `content`. If `i.content` is `nil`, calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, breaking feed polling. The code has no fallback to `description`/`content_encoded` or nil-guard, so this is a real correctness defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed has no per-item error isolation: one bad item aborts the whole poll, and combined with the embed_url unique index, items after the failing one are never imported

adjudication.rationale: This is a real issue in the diff. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` iterates `rss.items.each` and calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no per-item `rescue`, so any exception raised while processing one item (parsing content, `scrub`, network/HTML issues, or DB errors) will abort the whole poll and prevent later items from being imported in that run. Additionally, `topic_embeds.embed_url` has a unique index, but `TopicEmbed.import` uses a non-atomic check-then-create (`embed = ...first` then `TopicEmbed.create!`) and does not handle `RecordNotUnique`, so concurrent imports of the same URL can raise and, because PollFeed doesn’t isolate errors per item, terminate the loop early.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :topic_embeds, force: true is unnecessary and drops existing rows if the migration is re-run after a partial failure or bookkeeping mismatch

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb the migration uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which instructs Rails to drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. While migrations normally run once, this option is unnecessary for a new table and creates a concrete data-loss risk if the migration is re-run (e.g., schema bookkeeping mismatch, manual table creation, or partial/failed runs that still left the table behind).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redis throttle in TopicRetriever uses non-atomic setnx followed by expire; if the process dies between calls the key persists forever without TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that embed URL

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only afterward a TTL is applied via `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands and not atomic. If the process/thread dies or an exception occurs between the `setnx` and `expire`, the key can be left without an expiration, and future calls will see `setnx` return false and treat it as “retrieved recently” forever for that embed URL. This defect is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Origin check in embed.js uses substring match (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of exact equality, allowing lookalike origins like https://evil.co to pass when discourseUrl is https://evil.com

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler checks origin with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is a substring/prefix match against `discourseUrl`, not an exact origin comparison. As a result, if `discourseUrl` is `https://evil.com/`, an event with `e.origin` of `https://evil.co` will yield `indexOf(...) === 0` and pass the check, allowing a lookalike origin to send `postMessage` data (e.g., `discourse-resize`) to the embed script. This is a real, verifiable security/correctness issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook returns raw verbatim when cook_method == raw_html, allowing unsanitized third-party RSS content from PollFeed to be stored in posts.cooked and rendered with raw, causing stored XSS on the forum origin

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which in Discourse is where sanitization typically occurs). `Jobs::PollFeed` pulls third-party feed content (`i.content`) and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import` with only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`—no HTML sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, meaning the raw third-party HTML becomes `post.raw`, and `post.cooked` will effectively be that same raw HTML. The embed view (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`) renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, making stored XSS from feed content a direct, verifiable risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into single-quoted inline JS in embed.html.erb postMessage call, allowing script injection on the forum origin via a crafted referer URL

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the code interpolates `<%= request.referer %>` into a quoted JavaScript string, but in Rails `<%=` output is HTML-escaped by default (e.g., `'` becomes `'`, `<` becomes `<`). Inside a `<script>` tag, these entities are not decoded into executable characters, so they do not break out of the string or terminate the script tag, which defeats the claimed “script injection via crafted referer”. While using the full referer as `postMessage` targetOrigin is questionable for correctness/security (it should be an origin), the specific XSS/script-injection claim is not verifiably true from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped URL interpolated into the imported_from anchor HTML in TopicEmbed.imported_from, allowing HTML attribute/event injection since URL is only validated with a basic https?:// prefix check

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends HTML containing an anchor built via string interpolation: `"#{url}"` and passes it into `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)`. The only validation on `url` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows characters like `'`, `"`, spaces, or `>` after the scheme. A crafted URL such as `http://example.com' onmouseover='alert(1)` would pass the regex and break out of the `href` attribute, enabling HTML/attribute injection. This content is then stored as post `raw` with `cook_method: :raw_html`, and later rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, making it a verifiable XSS vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic SETNX followed by EXPIRE in TopicRetriever: a crash between the two calls leaves the key with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval of that embed URL

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` the throttling logic in `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two Redis operations are not atomic. If the process crashes, is killed, or errors after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` is executed, the key can be left without a TTL, causing `setnx` to keep failing on future attempts and thus `retrieved_recently?` to return `true` indefinitely for that `@embed_url` (permanently blocking retrieval). This is a concrete correctness issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed lacks per-item error handling: one malformed feed item (missing content, nil title, or duplicate embed_url race) raises an unrescued exception that aborts the entire run with retry: false, silently skipping all subsequent items

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `poll_feed` loops `rss.items.each` with no per-item rescue. It assumes fields exist: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` will raise if `i.content` is nil (NoMethodError on `scrub`). It also calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)`, which may raise on creation because `topic_embeds.embed_url` has a unique index and `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic `where(...).first` then `create!`, so a concurrent insert can trigger `RecordNotUnique` and abort the whole job. Since `sidekiq_options retry: false`, any such exception stops processing remaining items and the job will not be retried automatically.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js postMessage origin check uses substring matching (indexOf !== -1) instead of exact equality, a weak verification of e.origin
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the origin validation is done via substring matching (indexOf !== -1) rather than strict origin equality, which can be bypassed by attacker-controlled domains containing the trusted domain as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading view reloads every 30 seconds forever on unrecoverable retrieval failure, causing unbounded request/job churn per visitor with no backoff or terminal state

adjudication.rationale: Yes. When `EmbedController#best` can’t find an existing embed (`topic_id` is nil), it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `embed/loading`. The loading view contains JS that `document.location.reload()` every 30000ms with no limit/backoff/terminal state. If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., `TopicRetriever` can’t import due to missing `embed_by_username`, HTTP failure, parsing failure, etc.), each visitor will keep re-requesting `/embed/best` indefinitely, repeatedly enqueuing `retrieve_topic` jobs. Although `TopicRetriever` throttles retrieval to once per 60 seconds per URL, the controller still enqueues a job every 30 seconds, so the unbounded request/job churn concern is verifiable from the diff.
